summary: Round-2 verification of the TaNix Alpha 2.0 silent-freeze bug (30-48h) at /app/q-chart-fin/backend. Wrote 23 targeted tests in tests/test_freeze_fix_r2.py attacking the exact round-1 gap: a synchronous requests I/O path in the vendored pyquotex client that blocked the entire asyncio event loop (Telegram polling included). All 23 round-2 tests pass, all 39 round-1 tests in test_freeze_fix.py still pass, and the whole suite still shows exactly 29 pre-existing failures (same test IDs the round-1 report catalogued -- stale caption/emoji expectations, unrelated to the freeze fix). Round-2 changes are correctly implemented: (1) navigator.Browser.send_request unconditionally applies DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT=(15,45) via kwargs.setdefault and preserves any caller-supplied timeout; (2) login.Login.__call__ offloads get_token/get_profile via loop.run_in_executor (verified BOTH by source inspection AND behaviourally by asserting they ran on a different thread than the loop and that a concurrent heartbeat coroutine kept ticking through a 0.8s slow login -- max heartbeat gap < 0.35s, ticks >= 6); (3) login.Login._post offloads its send_request the same way; (4) login.Login.awaiting_pin raises RuntimeError mentioning 'interactive console' when sys.stdin is None or isatty()==False and never invokes builtins.input (spied) -- the interactive path is still reachable when isatty() is True; (5) bot._heartbeat advances _HEARTBEAT['loop'] and is cancellable; (6) bot._hard_watchdog is a plain daemon thread that calls os._exit(1) on a stale heartbeat with the event loop NOT running (proving loop-independence -- this is the round-1 gap the async watchdog could not fix), and does NOT exit when the heartbeat is refreshed (no restart loop); (7) bot.post_init starts TICKS + heartbeat task + async watchdog task + a daemon Thread(target=_hard_watchdog, daemon=True); bot.post_shutdown cancels both watchdog and heartbeat tasks and closes NOTIFY / stops TICKS. cmd_start source contains no reference to QX/TICKS/SM/ensure_connected -- confirms the RCA that 'no /start reply == loop blocked'.

minor.issue: Emits a PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning because _hard_watchdog is an infinite while-True loop and the spy raises SystemExit to abort it. Harmless -- the assertion (os._exit called with 1) still runs synchronously before the warning; the daemon thread is torn down at process exit.

Same 29 pre-existing failures as round-1 (test_messages.py, test_martingale_pnl.py, test_bot_units.py, test_channel_selection.py) -- stale caption/emoji expectations from before the owner-tag + <b> preservation change. Not caused by round-2 edits.

action_items: No code fix needed for the freeze bug -- both root causes (blocking HTTP with no timeout, sync work on the event loop, useless async-only watchdog) are correctly addressed and verified.
Optional cleanup: update the 29 stale pre-existing tests to the new caption / @BfsTraderQX / premium-emoji-preserved format, or mark them xfail so CI stays green.
critical_code_review_comments: navigator.Browser.send_request: kwargs.setdefault('timeout', DEFAULT_HTTP_TIMEOUT) is exactly the right idiom -- default applied, explicit caller value preserved. Verified with GET/POST/headers paths and an explicit timeout=5 case.

login.Login.__call__: get_token and get_profile are now awaited via loop.run_in_executor(None, ...); the surrounding _post already used run_in_executor in round 2 as well. This closes the exact RCA: `requests` I/O can no longer freeze Telegram polling.

login.Login.awaiting_pin: guard `if not sys.stdin or not sys.stdin.isatty()` raises RuntimeError with a clear operator-facing message. Previously input() would either block the event loop on a real tty or raise EOFError on /dev/null (only KeyboardInterrupt was caught) -- this is fixed and covered.

bot._hard_watchdog runs in a plain daemon thread on purpose; the round-1 async watchdog could never fire because it was frozen along with the loop. The new thread-based supervisor is the only piece that can rescue a synchronous freeze. Behavioural test confirms it exits with the loop not running.

bot.post_init correctly wires all three supervisors (heartbeat task, async watchdog task, daemon thread). bot.post_shutdown cancels both tasks; the daemon thread is intentionally not joined (it will be killed at process exit).
HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=1s, LOOP_STALL_LIMIT=300s, HARD_WATCHDOG_INTERVAL=30s -- reasonable ratios: watchdog wakes 10x per stall window, and 5 min of no-loop-tick is well past any legitimate slow work.

Minor nit (not blocking): the async _watchdog still calls sys.stdout.flush() before os._exit; when the loop is genuinely wedged this branch will never execute anyway -- the hard watchdog is the actual rescue path.

Minor nit (not blocking): login.Login.awaiting_pin still uses `code = input(input_message)` synchronously (guarded by isatty). If a developer ever runs it interactively while an event loop is active, input() will block the loop. In practice this path is only hit by a human CLI operator, so acceptable.

success_rate.backend: 100% of targeted tests (23/23 round-2, 39/39 round-1, 106/106 targeted regression); whole-suite = same 29 pre-existing failures as round 1, no new regressions

Do NOT run under xdist; several tests monkeypatch module-level globals (bot._HEARTBEAT, LOOP_STALL_LIMIT, TICKS, SM, HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL, HARD_WATCHDOG_INTERVAL) and race under parallel workers. The whole-suite `python -m pytest tests/ -q -n 0 --ignore=tests/test_charting_pricetag.py` currently shows exactly 29 pre-existing failures (same test IDs as round-1); any NEW test id failing is a regression to investigate. Warning: test_hard_watchdog_exits_on_blocked_loop leaves a PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning behind -- expected, harmless.
rca of the issue: Round-2 RCA (validated): The round-1 fixes addressed the WEBSOCKET path (bounded handshake, bounded join, close-old-api) and the qx.QuotexManager lock, but the LOGIN path was still synchronous. pyquotex/http/navigator.py Browser.send_request() did blocking requests I/O with no timeout, and pyquotex/http/login.py Login.__call__ awaited get_token()/get_profile() directly on the event loop. A half-open TCP to Quotex therefore froze the whole loop -- Telegram polling included, which is exactly why /start now gets no reply. asyncio.wait_for cannot cancel a synchronous call, so the round-1 timeouts in qx.py gave false confidence. Round-2 fix: (a) navigator sets a default (connect=15, read=45) timeout on every request; (b) login offloads get_token/get_profile/_post/awaiting_pin's send_request to run_in_executor so the loop keeps breathing; (c) awaiting_pin fails loud when non-interactive instead of calling input(); (d) a plain-thread _hard_watchdog runs os._exit(1) after 300s without a loop heartbeat so systemd Restart=always finally fires even for a fully-wedged loop. All four pieces verified by tests/test_freeze_fix_r2.py.
